title: Make It Readable
prompt:
Fix a deliberately uncomfortable page of text. Set:

- A `font-family` stack on `body` that ends with a generic family (`sans-serif` or `serif`).
- `line-height` on `body` as a bare number between 1.4 and 2.
- `h1` with a `font-size` in `rem`.
- Link color that is not the default (your choice) — keep the underline present (do not set text-decoration: none on links).
boilerplate:
A very dense article

This paragraph is cramped, single-spaced, and hard to track line by line. Readers abandon dense pages quickly, and low-vision readers abandon them faster.

A link that lost its affordance

tests.name: body font stack ends generic
tests.hint: font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; — the generic family is the safety net.

tests.name: healthy line-height
tests.hint: line-height: 1.6; — a unitless number multiplies the font size.

tests.name: rem heading size
tests.hint: font-size: 2rem; scales with the reader's settings.

tests.name: links keep their affordance
tests.hint: Underlines are how everyone recognizes links at a glance — style color, keep the affordance.
